title: Address-age criterion and the s.37a BDSG address-data exclusion
observation: From 20 Nov 2026, s.37a(2) No.1(d) BDSG allows a probability value to be created or used only if address data are not used; the committee report calls their use impermissible without exception (L01, L02). The old s.31(1) No.3 restricted only the exclusive use of address data; s.37a bans their use outright. Criterion 4, age of current address, carries up to 94 points. Two readings are open: a broad one, under which residence time is derived from address history and so falls under the ban, and a narrow one, under which the ban targets geographic location (geoscoring) and residence time is a stability measure. Commentators say no court has decided between them, and the bureau has not publicly explained its treatment; its 11 Nov 2026 announcement, as reported, deals with older scores and does not mention this criterion (L03, L21, V17).
condition: The bureau to give a written legal position on criterion 4 and confirm the exact model version Mainkai will receive after 20 Nov 2026. If the criterion changes, the bureau supplies the revised table and a score-migration analysis before cut-offs are set.
owner: Head of Legal with Head of Credit Risk
residual_risk: Legal uncertainty remains until a court or the data protection authority rules; contract warranty and re-calibration right reduce it. Residence time also correlates with age, which s.37a bans as an input, so the criterion may draw challenge on both grounds.
escalation: Becomes Critical if the bureau keeps the criterion unchanged and Mainkai's counsel concludes it is address data.

title: No outcomes evidence on Mainkai's own applicants
observation: The only public performance figure is a company-reported Gini of 0.6 with no sample, period, product or interval (V12). That figure is measured on the bureau's whole population and cannot be compared with a Gini on Mainkai's applicants, which is lower by construction. Mainkai's tolerance is therefore relative: on the same retro-scored applicants, the new score may not lose more than 3 Gini points against the current score (lower 95% bound of the paired difference), and must be calibrated within tolerance in every pricing band. Testing a new score version on a bank's own book needs the bureau to score the bank's historical applicants retrospectively (V20). The Bondora proxy run (section 3) demonstrates the paired test and rank ordering; its absolute Gini (0.37) is not comparable, because the sample holds approved loans only (B03).
condition: The bureau to retro-score a sample of Mainkai Ratenkredit applications (24 to 36 months, approvals and declines) with both the new and the current score. Mainkai Model Validation computes the paired Gini difference with a bootstrap interval, calibration by pricing band and class migration.
residual_risk: Back-testing covers approved loans only; reject inference remains a limitation.

title: Thin-file segments: calibration within segments not evidenced
observation: No segment performance is public, so nothing shows that a given score carries the same default risk for thin-file applicants as for everyone else. A lower score for a short credit history is expected by design; the open question is whether the score is calibrated within those segments. Context from the calculator: time-dependent criteria hold 280 of 999 points, and with perfect payment behaviour and no mortgage a person one year into the German credit file reaches at most 743 (Class 2); Class 1 takes between 2 and 5 years, depending on unpublished annual bands. A consumer score app that displays the score says less active persons may score somewhat worse (V18); the consumer federation expects young people to be more affected (L14). On Bondora's data, the same grade carried between 0.72 and 2.34 times the expected default risk across segments (section 3, B03).
condition: The bureau to provide score distribution, default rate by score band and Gini within each age band and time-in-file band, and its bias examination. Mainkai computes approval-rate ratios on retro-scored data before setting cut-offs.
residual_risk: Even with evidence, time-based criteria act as a partial age proxy; s.37a bans age as an input, not correlated inputs.

title: Points table incomplete for policy simulation
observation: Annual values are unpublished for bank-contract age (years 2 to 3, 5 to 9, 11 to 19), card age (years 2 to 4, 6 to 9) and address age (years 2 to 9). The debt-collection inquiry effect has no published value. Criteria 4, 5, 8 and 9 and the class boundaries were confirmed by the author on the bureau's own pages (V21, V22).
condition: The bureau to supply the complete band table with boundary and rounding rules under NDA.
residual_risk: Low once the table is supplied and version-controlled.

title: Independent review exists but its content is not available
observation: The bureau reports a Fraunhofer IAIS review confirming scientific quality and data relevance, a data protection authority finding of applicability, and review by two university departments (V12, V13). Scope, version reviewed, date and findings are not public.
condition: The bureau to provide the review reports or a summary letter stating scope, model version, date, findings and limitations.
residual_risk: Mainkai still owns effective challenge; the external review supplements it.

title: Target definition and development documentation not available
observation: The method (logistic regression, points from group default rates) is public (V12, V13). The target event, horizon, development and validation samples, exclusions and log-odds scaling are not. Fitness for unsecured instalment lending is not stated.
condition: The bureau to supply a development summary covering target, horizon, samples, exclusions, scaling and intended uses.
residual_risk: Low to medium once received; residual mismatch handled through Mainkai's own calibration.

title: Version and change management not evidenced
observation: Older sector models expire on 31 Dec 2028 and older scores were adjusted for s.37a (V17); further change to the new score is plausible (F01). No public policy defines material change, notice periods or parallel runs. A significant design change after 2 Dec 2027 would also bring the score under the AI Act (L08).
condition: Contract to require advance notice of model changes (at least 90 days), a material-change definition, parallel scoring, and re-validation evidence for each new version.
residual_risk: Medium: notice protects planning but not the outcome of a change.

title: Third-party classification and DORA contract baseline
observation: Since MaRisk 06/2026, ICT services under Art 3(21) DORA fall outside AT 9 (L11). Score delivery is an ongoing data service through ICT systems, so the most likely classification is a DORA ICT service supporting a critical or important function (credit origination). Under MaRisk, retrieving a standard bureau score is generally treated as other external procurement (sonstiger Fremdbezug, AT 9 Tz. 1), not outsourcing; AT 9 would matter only if the bureau built or ran a model customised to Mainkai's underwriting. Either way, the DORA classification sets the contract baseline. Contract, SLAs, assurance reports and exit terms are not public.
condition: Mainkai to document the classification, map the contract to Art 30(2) and (3), add the register-of-information entry and an exit plan that keeps origination running if the score is withdrawn.
residual_risk: Concentration risk on a dominant bureau remains; exit options are limited.

title: AI Act status contested; readiness plan needed
element: M; P1 to P10; D1 to D10
observation: Annex III point 5(b) targets credit scoring, and the bureau describes the method as learning from data (V12). The Commission's guidelines place logistic regression used to improve optimisation outside the definition (L09). The score was placed on the market in March 2026, so under Art 111(2) it is caught only after a significant design change following 2 Dec 2027 (L08).
condition: Adopt a precautionary in-scope position; contract for the bureau to supply Art 13 instructions for use, logging and incident information if the score becomes in scope; prepare a FRIA outline now.
residual_risk: Low: GDPR, s.37a BDSG and MaRisk already require most of the same controls.

title: Decline notices, explanation and contest route must meet ss.30(6)-(7) and 37a(5) BDSG
observation: Points per criterion allow a person-level explanation. From 20 Nov 2026, s.37a(5) gives applicants a right to contest and to a decision by a natural person against the lender (L04). The BGH held Art 15(1)(h) applies only where Art 22(1) is met, but a transmitted score followed by an adverse decision raises a presumption (L05). The act itself sets three lender duties for consumer loans (L01): under s.30(6), where the creditworthiness check is automated the borrower may demand human intervention, a clear explanation including the logic and risks, to state a view and a review, and must be told of these rights; under s.30(7) sentence 1, a rejection resulting from credit-agency information must be notified at once with the information received, details of the database consulted and the data categories considered; under s.30(7) sentence 2, a rejection resting on automated processing must also state the right to review by a person and the procedure to contest. Failing to inform under s.30(6) sentence 3 or s.30(7) is an administrative offence (s.43(1) No. 2 BDSG), and consumer associations can sue over ss.30 and 37a (s.2(2) No. 14 UKlaG as amended).
condition: Mainkai to rebuild decline letters and the underwriter review script around the 12 criteria, name the bureau database and data categories in every decline that rests on bureau information (s.30(7) sentence 1), state the right to review by a person and the contest procedure in every automated decline (sentence 2), and agree with the bureau the data-correction turnaround for disputed entries.
residual_risk: Low once notice templates are tested on real declines and reviewed by Legal before go-live.

title: Data quality and correction process not evidenced
observation: The bureau publishes the categories of data it stores and their deletion periods, for example inquiries after 12 months and settled claims after 3 years (V23). Data lineage, reporting coverage (for example which accounts count as bank contracts), quality KPIs and dispute volumes are not public. The consumer federation reports a correction of address-age data offered only against a paid registration certificate (L14).
condition: The bureau to provide data-quality KPIs, coverage by criterion and dispute statistics; contract a correction SLA.
residual_risk: Medium: data accuracy depends on reporting firms outside the bureau's control.

title: Monitoring pack and thresholds not yet defined
observation: Art 26(5) monitoring can be met through MaRisk governance, but needs the bureau population reports and Mainkai's own approval, override and default tracking by score band and segment. On Bondora's data the overall default rate was 8.3% in 2025 against 8.6% in the reference period, while seven of eight grades worsened, because the mix shifted to the best grade (section 3, B03).
condition: Mainkai to set PSI, approval-rate and override thresholds with owners; the bureau to supply quarterly population reports.

title: Mainkai's own loan moves its borrowers' scores
observation: In the calculator a 60-month Ratenkredit lowers the score by 78 to 88 points and a 96-month loan by 88 to 98, through three criteria at once (loans taken, remaining term, credit status). The under-25 archetype falls from Class 2 to Class 4.
condition: Mainkai to reflect own-exposure effects in top-up policy and monitoring, and to tell applicants how loan term affects their score.
residual_risk: Low; policy design issue rather than a model defect.

title: Consumer-facing reason texts
observation: The consumer federation reports generic replies to follow-up questions about score changes (L14).
condition: Agree a plain-German reason-text catalogue for the 12 criteria with the bureau.
